content: Children across the United States are typically seen at clinics an average of twice per year, during which their height and weight are measured. Between 1988 and 1997, a total of 246,371 children were examined, and 177,304 were included in the analysis. Overweight in 4-year-old children was defined as having a BMI-for-age greater than the 95th percentile based on the 2000 CDC growth reference. Underweight was defined as a BMI-for-age below the 5th percentile. In a sub-analysis, 12,587 mother-child pairs were included, contingent on the availability of pregnancy records. Exclusion criteria for this analysis included: (1) children for whom breastfeeding duration was not assessed, (2) children with inconsistent breastfeeding duration reports across visits, and (3) children lacking data on height, weight, gender, race/ethnicity, and birth weight. Breastfeeding duration was categorized into six groups: never, 1 month, 1–2 months, 3–5 months, 6–11 months, and 12 months or more. The CARDIA study, a U.S. multicenter prospective cohort study, examined cardiovascular disease risk trends in young Black and White men and women. Participants were recruited from four geographic areas: Birmingham, Alabama; Chicago, Illinois; Minneapolis, Minnesota; and Oakland, California. Exclusion criteria included diabetes, hysterectomy or oophorectomy, pregnancy or lactation at baseline, diabetes development before first birth, loss to follow-up, absence of post-baseline births, and missing lactation duration data. Women reported lactation duration for all previous births at year 7 and subsequent examinations. Lactation duration was calculated using midpoint values for each category and summed across all births. The prevalence of early childhood caries (ECC) was assessed in a study involving Aboriginal children in South Australia. The study included 307 children with data collected at baseline, 2 years, and 3 years of age. Breastfeeding duration was divided into four categories: never breastfed, breastfed for less than 12 months, breastfed for 12–23 months, and breastfed for 24 months or longer. ECC was defined as the presence of at least one decayed, missing, or filled tooth at 3 years of age. The severity of ECC was measured by the mean number of decayed, missing, and filled tooth surfaces. In a retrospective cohort study conducted in Myanmar, data were collected from mothers of 25to 30-month-old children. Children who were bottle-fed and breastfed from 5 months onward, as well as those who consumed jaggery (a caramel sugar), were excluded from further analysis. Breastfeeding duration was categorized into the first, second, and third years of life. Dental caries were assessed by a dentist using natural light and a mouth mirror, with caries defined as the presence of a visible cavity or softened cavity floor or wall. In a cross-sectional study in Seoul, Korea, parents of 15,515 children aged 0–13 years completed questionnaires on atopic dermatitis (AD), family history, and environmental factors. Current AD was defined as a positive response to three specific questions about itchy rashes. Breastfeeding duration was categorized as less than 6 months, 6–12 months, and more than 12 months. The study examined the effect of breastfeeding duration on current AD. The Southampton Women’s Survey (SWS) in the UK followed children born to women aged 20–34 years. Diet was assessed at 6 and 12 months using food frequency questionnaires (FFQs). Breastfeeding duration was recorded based on the date of the last breastfeed.
